def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-space:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix complex
scalars. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, bounded or
unbounded, and write $L^2(I;\mathbb C)$ for the complex Hilbert space of
Lebesgue (equivalence classes of) square-integrable functions with the inner
product $\langle u,v\rangle=\int_Iu\overline v$ linear in the first argument
([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]).

**First-order space.** Define
$H^1(I):=\{u\in L^2(I;\mathbb C):\ \text{the weak derivative }Du\text{ of the class }u\text{ exists and }Du\in L^2(I;\mathbb C)\},$
where $Du$ is the weak derivative of
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]: a class
$Du\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(I;\mathbb C)$ with
$\int_Iu\,\varphi'=(-1)\int_I(Du)\varphi\qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(I),$
an identity that is choice-free
([[def-locally-integrable-function-as-a-regular-distribution]]). Equip
$H^1(I)$ with the sesquilinear form
$\langle u,v\rangle_{H^1}:=\int_Iu\overline v+\int_I(Du)\overline{Dv},$
whose associated norm is $\|u\|_{H^1}=(\|u\|_{L^2}^2+\|Du\|_{L^2}^2)^{1/2}$;
the symbol $u'$ denotes the same weak derivative $Du$ throughout the page.

**Second-order space.** Define
$H^2(I):=\{u\in H^1(I):Du\in H^1(I)\},$
and for $u\in H^2(I)$ write $D^2u:=D(Du)\in L^2(I;\mathbb C)$; the norm is
$\|u\|_{H^2}=(\|u\|_{L^2}^2+\|Du\|_{L^2}^2+\|D^2u\|_{L^2}^2)^{1/2}$.
Thus $H^2(I)$ consists exactly of the classes in $L^2(I)$ whose first and
second weak derivatives exist and lie in $L^2(I)$, and $H^2(I)\subseteq
H^1(I)$.

**Endpoint-vanishing first-order space and the Dirichlet form.** For the
bounded interval $(0,L)$, $L>0$, define
$H^1_0(0,L):=\overline{C_c^\infty(0,L)}^{\,\|\cdot\|_{H^1}},$
the closure of the test functions in $H^1(0,L)$, and define the **Dirichlet
form** on it by $q_D[u]:=\|Du\|_{L^2(0,L)}^2=\int_0^L|Du|^2$.

**Elementary consequences, recorded for reuse.** Weak derivatives are unique
as locally integrable classes under Countable Choice, are additive and
$\mathbb C$-homogeneous, and classical derivatives of continuously
differentiable functions are weak derivatives. The cited published items
supply these facts, so $H^1(I)$ and $H^2(I)$ are well-defined linear
subspaces of $L^2(I;\mathbb C)$. No claim is made here that $H^1_0(0,L)$
equals the set of classes with vanishing endpoint values; that identification
is proved on this page from the trace estimates.
lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-re:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $-\infty<a<b<\infty$
and let $u\in H^1(a,b)$ have weak derivative $u'=Du$
([[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]). Then:

(a) there is exactly one representative $u^*$ of the class $u$ that is
continuous on $[a,b]$, is absolutely continuous on $[a,b]$, and satisfies
$u^*(x)-u^*(y)=\int_y^xu'(t)\,dt\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in[a,b],$
where for $x<y$ the right-hand side means $-\int_x^yu'$;

(b) for all $x,y\in[a,b]$,
$|u^*(x)-u^*(y)|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\;\|u'\|_{L^2(a,b)},$
so $u^*$ is uniformly continuous, and the assignment $u\mapsto u^*$ is linear;

(c) if additionally $u\in H^2(a,b)$, then $(u^*)'$ is absolutely continuous
on $[a,b]$ and $(u^*)'(x)-(u^*)'(y)=\int_y^xD^2u$ for all $x,y\in[a,b]$.
lem-nrqm-intervals-endpoint-trace-and-ha:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $u^*$ denote the continuous absolutely
continuous representative of a class in $H^1$ supplied by
[[lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-representative]], and write
$\|u\|=\|u\|_{L^2}$ and $\|u'\|=\|u'\|_{L^2}$ for the norms of
[[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]] on the interval under
consideration.

(a) *Bounded-interval trace bound.* Let $L>0$ and $u\in H^1(0,L)$. Then
$|u^*(x)|\le L^{-1/2}\|u\|_{L^2(0,L)}+L^{1/2}\|u'\|_{L^2(0,L)}
\qquad\text{for every }x\in[0,L].$
More generally, for $0\le c<d\le L$ and $x\in[c,d]$,
$|u^*(x)|\le(d-c)^{-1/2}\|u\|_{L^2(c,d)}+(d-c)^{1/2}\|u'\|_{L^2(c,d)} .$

(b) *Half-line.* Let $u\in H^1(0,\infty)$, with representative $u^*$ defined
on $[0,\infty)$ by gluing the representatives on $(0,n)$. Then
$|u^*(x)|\le\|u\|_{L^2(x,x+1)}+\|u'\|_{L^2(x,x+1)}\quad(x\ge0),\qquad
\sup_{x\ge0}|u^*(x)|\le\|u\|_{L^2(0,\infty)}+\|u'\|_{L^2(0,\infty)},$
and $u^*(x)\to0$ as $x\to\infty$.

(c) *Real line and vanishing boundary products.* Let $u,v\in H^1(\mathbb R)$
with continuous representatives $u^*,v^*$. Then $u^*,v^*$ are bounded and
uniformly continuous with
$|u^*(x)-u^*(y)|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\,\|u'\|_{L^2(\mathbb R)},\qquad
\sup_{\mathbb R}|u^*|\le\|u\|_{L^2(\mathbb R)}+\|u'\|_{L^2(\mathbb R)},$
$u^*(x)\to0$ and $v^*(x)\to0$ as $|x|\to\infty$, and consequently
$\lim_{|x|\to\infty}u^*(x)\overline{v^*(x)}=0$.
lem-nrqm-intervals-integration-by-parts:
## Statement

Assume the Axioms of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]).
Use the spaces of [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]] and the
absolutely continuous representatives supplied by
[[lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-representative]].

(a) *Bounded intervals.* Let $0<L<\infty$ and $u,v\in H^1(0,L)$. Then
$\int_0^Lu\,\overline{v'}=u^*(L)\overline{v^*(L)}-u^*(0)\overline{v^*(0)}
-\int_0^Lu'\,\overline v .$

(b) *Endpoint-vanishing space.* $H^1_0(0,L)=\{u\in H^1(0,L):u^*(0)=u^*(L)=0\}$,
with the traces $u^*(0),u^*(L)$ of the continuous representative.

(c) *Second-order identity.* For $u,v\in H^2(0,L)$,
$\int_0^L\bigl(u''\overline v-u\,\overline{v''}\bigr)
=\bigl[u'^*\overline{v^*}-u^*\overline{v'^*}\bigr]_0^L,$
where the bracket denotes
$u'^*(L)\overline{v^*(L)}-u^*(L)\overline{v'^*(L)}
-u'^*(0)\overline{v^*(0)}+u^*(0)\overline{v'^*(0)}$.

(d) *Half-line and line.* If $u,v\in H^1(0,\infty)$, then
$\int_0^\infty u\overline{v'}=-u^*(0)\overline{v^*(0)}-\int_0^\infty u'\overline v$, both integrals
being absolutely convergent. For $u,v\in H^1(\mathbb R)$ one instead has
$\int_{\mathbb R}u\overline{v'}=-\int_{\mathbb R}u'\overline v$,
with both integrals absolutely convergent.
thm-nrqm-intervals-sine-on-completeness:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$ and let
$L^2(0,L;\mathbb C)$ be as in [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]].
Define, for $n\ge1$,
$e_n(x):=\sqrt{\frac2L}\,\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr),\qquad x\in[0,L].$
Then $(e_n)_{n\ge1}$ is an orthonormal family and a complete orthonormal
family (Hilbert basis) of $L^2(0,L;\mathbb C)$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]):
$\langle e_n,e_m\rangle=\delta_{nm},\qquad
\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{e_n:n\ge1\}=L^2(0,L;\mathbb C).$
lem-nrqm-intervals-free-line-resolvent:
## Statement

Assume the Axioms of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $z\in\mathbb C\setminus[0,\infty)$ and let
$k\in\mathbb C$ be the unique complex number with $k^2=-z$ and $\operatorname{Re}k>0$.
Put
$G_z(t):=\frac{1}{2k}e^{-k|t|}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$
and let $A_0$ be the free one-dimensional operator of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) with $d=1$, $c=4\pi^2$ and $b=0$: $D(A_0)=H^2(\mathbb R)$ and
$A_0u=-D^2u$ for every $u\in H^2(\mathbb R)$, where $D^2$ is the second weak
derivative of [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]. Write
$\sigma:=\operatorname{Re}k>0$. Then:

(a) $G_z\in H^1(\mathbb R)\cap L^1(\mathbb R)\cap L^2(\mathbb R)$, its weak
derivative is the class of $t\mapsto-\tfrac12\operatorname{sgn}(t)e^{-k|t|}$,
and
$\|G_z\|_{L^1}=\frac{1}{|k|\sigma},\qquad
\|G_z\|_{L^2}=\frac{1}{2|k|\sqrt{\sigma}},\qquad
\|DG_z\|_{L^1}=\frac{1}{\sigma};$

(b) for every $f\in L^2(\mathbb R)$ the convolution
$u:=G_z*f$, $u(x)=\int_{\mathbb R}G_z(x-y)f(y)dy$, lies in $H^2(\mathbb R)$
with
$\|u\|_{L^2}\le\|G_z\|_{L^1}\|f\|_{L^2},\qquad
\|u\|_{L^\infty}\le\frac{1}{2|k|\sqrt\sigma}\|f\|_{L^2},$
and $A_0u-zu=f$;

(c) the linear map $R_0(z):L^2(\mathbb R)\to L^2(\mathbb R)$, $f\mapsto G_z*f$
is bounded with range exactly $H^2(\mathbb R)$, and
$(A_0-z)R_0(z)=I_{L^2},\qquad R_0(z)(A_0-z)=I_{H^2};$
in particular $R_0(z)=(A_0-z)^{-1}$ and $A_0-z$ is a bijection from $H^2(\mathbb R)$
onto $L^2(\mathbb R)$;

(d) $(-\tfrac{d^2}{dx^2}-z)G_z=\delta_0$ in the sense of distributions: for
every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$,
$\int_{\mathbb R}G_z(x)\bigl(-\varphi''(x)-z\varphi(x)\bigr)dx=\varphi(0).$
thm-nrqm-intervals-dirichlet-diagonal-do:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$, let
$e_n(x)=\sqrt{\tfrac2L}\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr),\qquad
\lambda_n:=\Bigl(\frac{n\pi}{L}\Bigr)^2\quad(n\ge1),$
let $(e_n)_{n\ge1}$ be the complete orthonormal family of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-sine-on-completeness]], and let $A_D$ be the diagonal
operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]]
associated with $(e_n)$ and $(\lambda_n)$: $A_Dx=\sum_{n\ge1}\lambda_n
\langle x,e_n\rangle e_n$ with domain
$D(A_D)=\Bigl\{x\in L^2(0,L;\mathbb C):\sum_{n\ge1}\lambda_n^2|\langle x,e_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$
Let $B$ be the Dirichlet Laplacian
$Bu:=-D^2u,\qquad D(B)=\{u\in H^2(0,L):u^*(0)=u^*(L)=0\},$
with $H^2$ and the trace $u^*$ of [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]
and [[lem-nrqm-intervals-integration-by-parts]] clause (b). Then:

(a) $D(A_D)=D(B)$ and $A_D=B$; in particular $D(A_D)$ is a linear subspace of
$H^2(0,L)$ whose members have vanishing endpoint traces;

(b) $A_D$ is self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]),
positive, and its spectrum is $\sigma(A_D)=\{\lambda_n:n\ge1\}$; each
$\lambda_n$ is an eigenvalue with eigenvector $e_n$; the eigenvalues are
simple in the sense that $\ker(A_D-\lambda_n)$ contains no vector orthogonal
to $e_n$;

(c) for every $u\in D(A_D)$, $\langle A_Du,u\rangle=\|Du\|_{L^2(0,L)}^2$;
consequently $A_D\ge\lambda_1=(\pi/L)^2$ in the quadratic-form sense on its
domain.
lem-nrqm-intervals-compact-resolvent-eig:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on an
infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $H$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-dimension]]), let $c\in\mathbb R$ lie in the
resolvent set of $A$, and assume that the resolvent
$R_c:=(A-c)^{-1}\in\mathcal B(H)$ is compact
([[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-compact-linear-operator]]). Then:

(a) $H$ has a complete orthonormal family $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of
eigenvectors of $A$; writing $\mu_n$ for the eigenvalue of $e_n$, one has
$|\mu_n|\to\infty$ (each eigenvalue repeated according to its finite
multiplicity), and every eigenspace of $A$ is finite dimensional;

(b) $\sigma(A)$ consists exactly of the eigenvalues $\mu_n$ of $A$ and has no
other points, and the essential spectrum is empty:
$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)=\varnothing$
([[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]]); thus
every spectral point of $A$ is an isolated eigenvalue of finite
multiplicity;

(c) for every $z$ in the resolvent set of $A$ the resolvent $(A-z)^{-1}$ is
compact.
thm-nrqm-intervals-twisted-periodic-mome:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$ and $\theta\in[0,2\pi)$. Put
$D_\theta:=\{u\in H^1(0,L):u^*(L)=e^{i\theta}u^*(0)\},\qquad
P_\theta u:=-i\,Du,$
with $H^1$ and the trace $u^*$ of [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]
and [[lem-nrqm-intervals-integration-by-parts]] clause (b). Then:

(a) $D_\theta$ is dense in $L^2(0,L;\mathbb C)$, $P_\theta$ is symmetric and
self-adjoint;

(b) the functions
$\varphi_n(x):=\frac{1}{\sqrt L}e^{i(2\pi n+\theta)x/L}\qquad(n\in\mathbb Z)$
form a complete orthonormal family of $L^2(0,L;\mathbb C)$, each
$\varphi_n\in D_\theta$, and $P_\theta\varphi_n=\kappa_n\varphi_n$ with
$\kappa_n:=\frac{2\pi n+\theta}{L};$
the eigenvalues $\kappa_n$ are simple and
$\sigma(P_\theta)=\{\kappa_n:n\in\mathbb Z\}$;

(c) $P_\theta$ is the unique self-adjoint extension of the symmetric operator
$P_\theta$ restricted to the finite linear span of the $\varphi_n$, and its
domain is exactly
$D_\theta=\Bigl\{\sum_nc_n\varphi_n:\sum_n\kappa_n^2|c_n|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$
thm-nrqm-intervals-bounded-interval-pert:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$, let $A_D$ be the Dirichlet
Laplacian of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-dirichlet-diagonal-domain-identification]] with
$D(A_D)=\{u\in H^2(0,L):u^*(0)=u^*(L)=0\}$ and $A_Du=-D^2u$, and let
$V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$ with $\|V\|_\infty=\max_{[0,L]}|V|$. Let
$A:=A_D+M_V$ with domain $D(A):=D(A_D)$, where $(M_Vu)=Vu$ is multiplication
by $V$. Then:

(a) $M_V$ is bounded self-adjoint with $\|M_V\|=\|V\|_\infty$, $A$ is
self-adjoint on $D(A_D)$, and $Au=-D^2u+Vu$ for $u\in D(A_D)$;

(b) $A$ has compact resolvent: $(A-z)^{-1}$ is compact for every
$z\in\rho(A)$; consequently $A$ has a complete orthonormal family of
eigenvectors, all eigenspaces are finite dimensional, the eigenvalues
$E_1\le E_2\le\cdots$ (listed with multiplicity) satisfy $E_n\to\infty$ and
$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)=\varnothing$;

(c) with $\lambda_n=(n\pi/L)^2$ and $E_n(A_D)=\lambda_n$, the min-max
eigenvalues satisfy
$\bigl|E_n-\lambda_n\bigr|\le\|V\|_\infty\qquad(n\ge1).$
thm-nrqm-intervals-regular-ivp-parameter:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$ and let
$V\in C([0,L];\mathbb C)$ with $M:=\|V\|_{C^0}=\max_{[0,L]}|V|$. For
$z\in\mathbb C$, $x_0\in[0,L]$ and $c_0,c_1\in\mathbb C$ consider the
initial value problem
$\text{(IVP)}\qquad -u''+Vu=zu,\qquad u(x_0)=c_0,\quad u'(x_0)=c_1,$
for $u\in C^2([0,L];\mathbb C)$. Then:

(a) (IVP) has exactly one solution $u(\cdot\,;z,x_0,c_0,c_1)$; it is the
unique continuous solution of the Volterra equation
$u(x)=c_0+c_1(x-x_0)+\int_{x_0}^x(x-t)\bigl(V(t)-z\bigr)u(t)\,dt
\qquad(x\in[0,L]),$
the integral over $[x_0,x]$ for $x<x_0$ carrying the negative orientation, and
$\sup_{[0,L]}|u|\le\bigl(|c_0|+|c_1|L\bigr)e^{(M+|z|)L^2};$

(b) for fixed $x_0,c_0,c_1$ and $R>0$, the map
$[0,L]\times[-R,R]\to\mathbb C\times\mathbb C$, $(x,z)\mapsto\bigl(u(x;z),u'(x;z)\bigr)$
is continuous, is differentiable in $z$, and its $z$-derivative
$w:=\partial_zu(\cdot\,;z)$ is the unique $C^2$ solution on $[0,L]$ of
$-w''+Vw-zw=u(\cdot\,;z),\qquad w(x_0)=0,\quad w'(x_0)=0 .$
In particular $w$ satisfies the associated Volterra equation
$w(x)=\int_{x_0}^x(x-t)\bigl[(V(t)-z)w(t)-u(t)\bigr]dt$.
thm-nrqm-intervals-prufer-energy-monoton:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$ and let
$V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$. For $E\in\mathbb R$ let $u(\cdot,E)$ be the unique
$C^2$ solution of
$-u''+Vu=Eu,\qquad u(0,E)=0,\quad u'(0,E)=1,$
supplied by [[thm-nrqm-intervals-regular-ivp-parameter-series]] (with
$x_0=0$, $c_0=0$, $c_1=1$). Put
$r(x,E):=\bigl(u(x,E)^2+u'(x,E)^2\bigr)^{1/2}>0,\qquad
\theta(x,E):=\int_0^x\frac{u'(t,E)^2-u(t,E)u''(t,E)}{u(t,E)^2+u'(t,E)^2}\,dt .$
Then:

(a) $u=r\sin\theta$ and $u'=r\cos\theta$ on $[0,L]\times\mathbb R$, $\theta$ is
$C^1$ in $x$ with $\theta(0,E)=0$ and
$\partial_x\theta(x,E)=\cos^2\theta(x,E)+\bigl(E-V(x)\bigr)\sin^2\theta(x,E);$

(b) for every $x\in(0,L]$ the map $E\mapsto\theta(x,E)$ is differentiable on
$\mathbb R$ with
$\partial_E\theta(x,E)=\int_0^x\frac{u(t,E)^2}{u(t,E)^2+u'(t,E)^2}\,dt>0;$
in particular $E\mapsto\theta(L,E)$ is continuous and strictly increasing on
$\mathbb R$, and $E\mapsto\theta(x,E)$ is continuous on $[0,L]\times\mathbb R$;

(c) for every $E$, $\theta(x,E)>0$ for $0<x\le L$; whenever
$\theta(x_0,E)=k\pi$ for some $k\in\mathbb Z$ and $x_0\in(0,L]$, one has
$\partial_x\theta(x_0,E)=1$ and $\theta(x,E)>k\pi$ for all $x\in(x_0,L]$; if
additionally $0<k\pi<\theta(L,E)$, then the level $k\pi$ is attained at exactly
one point of $(0,L)$.
thm-nrqm-intervals-dirichlet-nodal-theor:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$ and let
$V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$, with $V_{\min}:=\min_{[0,L]}V$ and
$V_{\max}:=\max_{[0,L]}V$. For $E\in\mathbb R$ let $u(\cdot,E)$ be the
solution of $-u''+Vu=Eu$, $u(0)=0$, $u'(0)=1$, and let $\theta(\cdot,E)$ be
its Prufer angle, as in [[thm-nrqm-intervals-prufer-energy-monotonicity]].
Call $E$ a **Dirichlet eigenvalue** when there is a nonzero
$w\in H^2(0,L)$ ([[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]) with
$w^*(0)=w^*(L)=0$ satisfying $-w''+Vw=Ew$, $w^*$ the continuous
representative of [[lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-representative]].
Then:

(a) $E$ is a Dirichlet eigenvalue if and only if $\theta(L,E)=k\pi$ for some
integer $k\ge1$;

(b) for every $k\ge1$ the equation $\theta(L,E)=k\pi$ has exactly one
solution $E_k$; the sequence $(E_k)_{k\ge1}$ is strictly increasing,
$E_k\to\infty$, and it is exactly the sequence of Dirichlet eigenvalues, each
with one-dimensional eigenspace:
$\ker(-\tfrac{d^2}{dx^2}+V-E_k)=\mathbb Cu(\cdot,E_k)$;

(c) bounds: for every $k\ge1$,
$\Bigl(\frac{k\pi}{L}\Bigr)^2+V_{\min}\le E_k\le
\Bigl(\frac{k\pi}{L}\Bigr)^2+V_{\max};$

(d) nodal count: for every $E$, the number of zeros of $u(\cdot,E)$ in
$(0,L]$ equals $\lfloor\theta(L,E)/\pi\rfloor$; consequently the $k$-th
eigenfunction $u(\cdot,E_k)$ has exactly $k-1$ zeros in $(0,L)$, and the same
holds for every nonzero eigenfunction with eigenvalue $E_k$.
thm-nrqm-intervals-delta-interface-opera:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\alpha\in\mathbb R$. Let $D(A_\alpha)$ be
the set of classes $u\in H^1(\mathbb R)$ whose restrictions to $(0,\infty)$
and $(-\infty,0)$ have representatives of class $H^2$ on each half-line
([[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]) and which satisfy the
**interface condition**
$u'^*(0+)-u'^*(0-)=\alpha\,u^*(0),$
where $u^*$ is the continuous representative of [[lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-representative]]
and $u'^*(0\pm)$ are the one-sided traces of the representative of the weak
derivative, which exist by
[[lem-nrqm-intervals-endpoint-trace-and-half-line-decay]]. For
$u\in D(A_\alpha)$ define $A_\alpha u$ to be the class equal to $-D^2u$ on
each half-line. Then:

(a) $D(A_\alpha)$ is a dense linear subspace of $L^2(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$
and $A_\alpha:D(A_\alpha)\to L^2(\mathbb R)$ is a well-defined linear
operator;

(b) $A_\alpha$ is symmetric;

(c) $A_\alpha$ is self-adjoint; explicitly, for $z\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R$
the operator $A_\alpha-z$ is a bijection $D(A_\alpha)\to L^2(\mathbb R)$.
thm-nrqm-intervals-delta-rank-one-resolv:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\alpha\in\mathbb R$ and let $A_\alpha$ be the
self-adjoint delta interface operator of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-delta-interface-operator]]; write $A_0$ for the
operator with $\alpha=0$, so that $D(A_0)=H^2(\mathbb R)$ and
$A_0u=-D^2u$. For $z\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R$ let $k$ with $k^2=-z$,
$\operatorname{Re}k>0$, let $G_z(t)=(2k)^{-1}e^{-k|t|}$, and define the
bounded linear functional
$\ell_z(f):=\int_{\mathbb R}G_z(y)f(y)\,dy\qquad(f\in L^2(\mathbb R)).$
Then for every $z\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R$:

(a) $1+\alpha G_z(0)=1+\alpha/(2k)\ne0$, and
$(A_\alpha-z)^{-1}f=(A_0-z)^{-1}f-\frac{\alpha\,\ell_z(f)}{1+\alpha G_z(0)}\,G_z
\qquad(f\in L^2(\mathbb R));$

(b) the difference
$K_z:=(A_\alpha-z)^{-1}-(A_0-z)^{-1}$ is a bounded operator of rank at most one (rank one if $\alpha\ne0$, and zero if $\alpha=0$),
$K_zf=-\dfrac{\alpha}{1+\alpha G_z(0)}\,\ell_z(f)\,G_z$, its range is
contained in $\mathbb C G_z$, and
$\|K_z\|\le\frac{|\alpha|\,\|G_z\|_{L^2}^2}{|1+\alpha G_z(0)|}
=\frac{|\alpha|}{4|k|^2\operatorname{Re}k\,\bigl|1+\alpha/(2k)\bigr|}\,;$
consequently
$\bigl\|(A_\alpha-z)^{-1}\bigr\|\le
\bigl\|(A_0-z)^{-1}\bigr\|+|K_z\| .$
thm-nrqm-intervals-delta-unique-bound-st:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\alpha\in\mathbb R$ and let $A_\alpha$ be the
self-adjoint delta interface operator of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-delta-interface-operator]] on
$L^2(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$. Then:

(a) $A_\alpha$ has no negative eigenvalue when $\alpha\ge0$; and $E=0$ is
not an eigenvalue of $A_\alpha$ for any $\alpha\in\mathbb R$;

(b) if $\alpha<0$, then $E_\alpha:=-\alpha^2/4<0$ is an eigenvalue of
$A_\alpha$ with one-dimensional eigenspace
$\ker(A_\alpha-E_\alpha)=\mathbb C\,\psi_\alpha,\qquad
\psi_\alpha(x):=\sqrt{-\tfrac\alpha2}\,e^{\alpha|x|/2};$
the vector $\psi_\alpha$ satisfies $\|\psi_\alpha\|=1$ and is the unique
negative eigenvalue, that is, if $E<0$ and $A_\alpha u=Eu$ for some
$u\in D(A_\alpha)$, then $E=E_\alpha$ and $u\in\mathbb C\psi_\alpha$;

(c) scaling: for any $\hbar,m>0$, the operator
$H_\alpha:=(\hbar^2/2m)A_\alpha$ on the same domain is self-adjoint,
$H_\alpha\psi_\alpha=E_{H}\psi_\alpha$ with
$E_H=-\hbar^2\alpha^2/(8m)$, and, writing $g:=\hbar^2\alpha/(2m)$, one has
$E_H=-mg^2/(2\hbar^2)$.
thm-nrqm-intervals-separated-robin-green:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$, let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$,
let $V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$, and put
$D(A):=\{u\in H^2(0,L):u'^*(0)=\alpha u^*(0),\ u'^*(L)=\beta u^*(L)\},\qquad
Au:=-D^2u+Vu,$
with $H^2$, weak derivatives and traces as in
[[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]] and
[[lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-representative]]. Then:

(a) $D(A)$ is dense in $L^2(0,L;\mathbb C)$, $A$ is well defined and
symmetric, and $A$ is self-adjoint;

(b) for every $z\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R$ there are unique $C^2$
solutions $u_a(\cdot,z)$ of $-u''+Vu=zu$ with
$u_a(0)=1$, $u_a'(0)=\alpha$, and $u_b(\cdot,z)$ with
$u_b(L)=1$, $u_b'(L)=\beta$; the Wronskian
$W(z):=u_a(x,z)u_b'(x,z)-u_a'(x,z)u_b(x,z)$
is independent of $x$ and $W(z)\ne0$;

(c) for $f\in L^2(0,L)$ the function
$u(x):=\int_0^LG_z(x,y)f(y)\,dy,\qquad
G_z(x,y):=-\frac{u_a(\min\{x,y\},z)\,u_b(\max\{x,y\},z)}{W(z)},$
lies in $H^2(0,L)$, satisfies the two Robin boundary conditions, and
$(A-z)u=f$. Consequently $(A-z)^{-1}f=u$, the resolvent is an integral
operator with continuous kernel $G_z$ on $[0,L]^2$, and $(A-z)^{-1}$ is a
compact operator for every $z$ in the resolvent set of $A$.
thm-nrqm-intervals-robin-simple-complete:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$, $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$,
$V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$, and let $A$ be the Robin realisation of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-separated-robin-green-resolvent]]:
$D(A)=\{u\in H^2(0,L):u'^*(0)=\alpha u^*(0),\ u'^*(L)=\beta u^*(L)\},\qquad
Au=-D^2u+Vu .$
Then:

(a) $A$ has compact resolvent; there is a complete orthonormal family
$(\psi_n)_{n\ge1}$ of eigenvectors of $A$, every eigenspace of $A$ is
one-dimensional, and the spectrum of $A$ consists exactly of the eigenvalues
$\lambda_n$ of $A$, listed with multiplicity, which satisfy
$\lambda_n\to\infty$ and $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)=\varnothing$;

(b) in particular the eigenvalues can be listed strictly increasingly as
$\lambda_1<\lambda_2<\cdots$ (each simple), and if $A\psi=\lambda\psi$ with
$\psi\ne0$, then $\psi$ is a nonzero multiple of the solution $u_a(\cdot,\lambda)$
of $-u''+Vu=\lambda u$, $u(0)=1$, $u'(0)=\alpha$, and the eigenvalue
condition is $\beta=\tfrac{u_a'(L,\lambda)}{u_a(L,\lambda)}$ when
$u_a(L,\lambda)\ne0$, while $u_a(L,\lambda)=0$ occurs for no eigenvalue.
thm-nrqm-intervals-barrier-transfer-and-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $a>0$, let
$U>E>0$ and $m,\hbar>0$, and put
$k:=\frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{\hbar}>0,\qquad
\kappa:=\frac{\sqrt{2m(U-E)}}{\hbar}>0 .$
Consider bounded functions $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ that are $C^1$ on
$\mathbb R$, twice continuously differentiable on each of $(-\infty,0)$,
$(0,a)$, $(a,\infty)$, and satisfy
$-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\psi''+V\psi=E\psi,\qquad
V(x)=\begin{cases}U,&0<x<a,\\0&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}$
on each of the three intervals. Then:

(a) exactly one such $\psi$ has the *transmission asymptotics*: its
restriction to $(-\infty,0)$ equals $e^{ikx}+re^{-ikx}$ and its restriction
to $(a,\infty)$ equals $te^{ikx}$, for uniquely determined $r,t\in\mathbb C$;

(b) with $D:=2\cosh(\kappa a)+i\bigl(\tfrac{\kappa}{k}-\tfrac{k}{\kappa}\bigr)\sinh(\kappa a)$,
$t=\frac{2e^{-ika}}{D},\qquad
T:=|t|^2=\Bigl[1+\frac{U^2\sinh^2(\kappa a)}{4E(U-E)}\Bigr]^{-1},\qquad
R:=|r|^2=1-T ;$

(c) with $q:=e^{-2\kappa a}$ and $C:=U^2/\bigl(4E(U-E)\bigr)$,
$T=\frac{(4/C)\,q}{1+\bigl(\tfrac4C-2\bigr)q+q^2}\,;$
consequently, whenever $\delta:=\bigl(\tfrac4C-2\bigr)q+q^2$ satisfies
$|\delta|\le\tfrac12$,
$\Bigl|T-\frac{16E(U-E)}{U^2}\,q\Bigr|\le\frac{32E(U-E)}{U^2}\,q\,|\delta| .$

No $L^2$ normalisation is asserted: $\psi$ is a bounded generalised solution,
not an element of $L^2(\mathbb R)$.
thm-nrqm-intervals-finite-well-root-cond:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $a>0$, $U>0$, $m,\hbar>0$ and put
$K:=\sqrt{2mU}/\hbar>0$. Let $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $V(x)=-U$ for
$|x|<a$ and $V(x)=0$ for $|x|>a$, and let
$H\psi:=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\psi''+V\psi,\qquad D(H):=H^2(\mathbb R),$
with $H^2$ of [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

(a) $H$ is self-adjoint on $H^2(\mathbb R)$;

(b) *root conditions.* $E\in\mathbb R$ with $-U<E<0$ is an eigenvalue of $H$
if and only if, writing $E=-\varepsilon$, $\kappa:=\sqrt{2m\varepsilon}/\hbar$
and $k:=\sqrt{2m(U-\varepsilon)}/\hbar$ (so that $k,\kappa>0$ and
$k^2+\kappa^2=K^2$), the pair $(k,\kappa)$ satisfies
$k\tan(ka)=\kappa\qquad\text{(even case)}\qquad\text{or}\qquad
-k\cot(ka)=\kappa\qquad\text{(odd case)} .$
Every such eigenvalue is simple, and its eigenfunction is, up to a nonzero
scalar, $x\mapsto\cos(kx)$ on $(-a,a)$ continued by $ce^{-\kappa|x|}$ outside
in the even case and $x\mapsto\sin(kx)$ on $(-a,a)$ continued by
$c\,\operatorname{sgn}(x)e^{-\kappa|x|}$ outside in the odd case;

(c) *range of energies.* There are no eigenvalues $E\le-U$ and no eigenvalues
$E\ge0$; hence all eigenvalues of $H$ lie in $(-U,0)$ and are given by (b);

(d) *bound count.* The number of negative eigenvalues of $H$ equals
$\Bigl\lceil\frac{2aK}{\pi}\Bigr\rceil,$
and more precisely the equations of (b) have exactly one solution $k$ in each
interval $\bigl(\frac{n\pi}{2a},\frac{(n+1)\pi}{2a}\bigr)$, $n\ge0$, whose
left endpoint satisfies $\frac{n\pi}{2a}<K$, and no solution in $(0,K)$
elsewhere; the solutions are alternatively of even type ($n$ even) and odd
type ($n$ odd).
